verdicts.evidence: Before we go any further, I just need to let you know this call is recorded for quality and training purposes. Is that all right with you?
verdicts.reason: The agent disclosed the call recording within the first minute, and the customer acknowledged it after the agent repeated it.

verdicts.evidence: Thanks, <PERSON>. That matches what I have here, so that's all confirmed.
verdicts.reason: The agent asked for full name and date of birth at 00:39 before looking at any details, and confirmed them before discussing the customer's situation or any quote.

verdicts.evidence: Would you mind telling me a bit about your situation and what made you look into life cover?
verdicts.reason: The agent asked about the customer's circumstances and reasons for wanting cover before recommending any cover amount or product.

verdicts.evidence: For the first two years after you start the policy, the stroke, and anything caused by it, wouldn't be covered.
verdicts.reason: The two-year pre-existing condition exclusion, stepped premiums, cover range, terminal illness benefit and 30-day full refund were all described consistently with the product facts.

verdicts.evidence: There's no pressure at all to decide today, and nothing changes if you take your time.
verdicts.reason: The agent explicitly said there was no pressure to decide, offered a call back and did not create false urgency.

verdicts.evidence: But I don't think I want to decide today.
verdicts.reason: No sale was completed on the call, so explicit consent before completing a sale does not apply.

verdicts.evidence: Would you like me to call back at a time when <PERSON> can be with you, so he can hear it too and ask any questions?
verdicts.reason: The customer disclosed a recent stroke, muddled words and money worries; the agent said there was absolutely no rush, slowed down, checked understanding, gave a recap and offered a call back with her husband.
Doesn't apply in the NZ market.
